scope: Isolated static high-gamma reflex circuit using native ARM neuron-update source, dense homogeneous populations and explicit initial conditions. This is not a full gait, FPGA or Webots test.
result: All eight tilt directions recruited the expected knee extensor readouts; bursts cleared and could retrigger from sustained sensory evidence. Single cues ended, flexion was vetoed during extension, and REST suppressed the circuit.
limitations: Gait pathways and STDP3 are excluded. A synthetic flexion stimulus tests opposition; learned gait inhibition could still defeat or alter the reflex on hardware.
The harness uses shared homogeneous state within dense populations, actual population widths and native cell updates. It is not a compiled image or FPGA transport timing test.
No ground contact, mechanical load or robot physics was simulated. Five-frame bursts in these cases do not guarantee balance or a completed servo stroke.
Internal readouts are bistable states, not spike telemetry or proof of dopaminergic firing.
